acceptanceCriteria: An accepted spec defines the hunk classes, the exact equivalence test for NON_SEMANTIC, and the UNCLASSIFIED fallback.
For Go files, a hunk that changes only comments or whitespace is reported NON_SEMANTIC; any token change outside comments (including build tags and //go: directives) is not.
Unsupported languages, parse failures and generated files are reported UNCLASSIFIED with a reason, never NON_SEMANTIC.
The reviewer report shows the class per hunk; tests cover comment-only, directive-change, mixed and unparsable fixtures.
body: Idea source: Anthropic engineering post 'Redesigning source control' (anthropic.com/engineering/redesigning-source-control), reviewed 2026-10-16. Idea only; no text copied. Scion's approval rules distinguish comment-only changes from sensitive logic changes, and reviewers concentrate on change intent. Corvint's reviewer report and CEM give every hunk the same review weight; there is no deterministic class for comment-only, whitespace-only or doc-string-only hunks. Idea: a deterministic, language-aware (Go first) hunk classifier that marks a hunk NON_SEMANTIC only when the parsed AST/token stream outside comments is byte-identical between base and head, recorded in the reviewer report (and, if accepted, as a CEM field) with an explanation. Missing parser support or any ambiguity yields UNCLASSIFIED, never NON_SEMANTIC (invariant 2). Project-owned authority decides what a class permits; the classifier itself grants no approval (invariant 3). Related: V1-0195 hunk-anchored review projection, V1-0820 project-owned reviewer rubric. Needs a spec (requirements, failure modes, rollback) before implementation.
title: cem report: classify comment-only and other non-semantic hunks so review effort and approval rules can differ by change class
